sentences.text: It is jointly submitted that parties have resolved the  dispute.
The complainant has no objection for quashing the  FIR.
4. Complainant is present in the Court.
She has expressed  her consent for quashing the FIR.
She is represented by the  Advocate.
She has filed affidavit of consent for quashing the  impugned FIR.
5. In the affidavit it is stated that complainant has cordially  resolved all the disputes with the accused and amicably settled  the dispute.

She do not want to pursue the criminal  proceedings against the petitioner as she intents to get  married and live in peace and move ahead in life and pursue  her career.
 6.
We have perused the FIR.
From the tenor of the FIR it  appears that there was consensual relationship between  accused and victim on several occasions.

7. Considering the fact that the parties have resolved the  dispute and affidavit filed by the complainant giving no  objection for quashing the FIR, the relief sought in this petition  can be granted.

sentences.text:

 35-WP-719-2024.odt  ORDER
(i) Writ Petition is allowed.

(ii) The proceedings in FIR dated 5.01.2024 registered with Malad Police Station vide Crime No. 16 of 2022 for offence under Sections 376 (2)(n), 417, 506 of the Indian Penal Code is quashed and set aside.
(iii) The petitioner shall pay cost of Rs. 2,50,000/- to Advocates Association of Western India Generation Next.
(iv) The details of the bank account for payment of costs are as under :
 Bank Name : Bank of India.
 Branch Name : Mumbai Main  Account No. : 000110110007807  IFSC Code : BKID0000001.
 (v) Petitioner to deposit the said cost of Rs. 2,50,000/- within a period of four weeks from today and submit the receipt of the same in the Registry of this Court.
( N.R. BORKAR, J.) (PRAKASH D. NAIK, J.)
